Package edu.cnu.mdi.splot.plot

Class PlotCanvas

java.lang.Object
java.awt.Component
java.awt.Container
javax.swing.JComponent
edu.cnu.mdi.splot.plot.PlotCanvas
All Implemented Interfaces:
DataChangeListener, ImageObserver, MenuContainer, Serializable, EventListener
public class PlotCanvas extends JComponent implements DataChangeListener
The primary Swing component for rendering a 2-D scientific plot.

Responsibilities

  • Owning the coordinate-system geometry (_worldSystem, setWorldSystem(), affine transforms)
  • Painting: delegating to DataDrawer, PlotTicks, Legend, and ExtraText
  • Notifying PlotChangeListeners on lifecycle events
  • Providing the public coordinate-conversion API (screen ↔ raw-world ↔ data)
  • Data management: setPlotData(edu.cnu.mdi.splot.pdata.PlotData), clearData()

Mouse handling

All mouse interaction (legend dragging, feedback readout, scroll-wheel zoom) is delegated to PlotMouseHandler, which is wired up in the constructor. PlotCanvas no longer implements any mouse listener interfaces directly.

Coordinate systems

Three coordinate spaces are in play:

  1. Screen (local) — Swing pixel coordinates, (0,0) at top-left.
  2. Raw world — stored in _worldSystem; log₁₀(data) when a log axis is active.
  3. Data — the real values in the curves, always linear.

Conversion methods are named screen*, *RawWorld*, and *Data* to make the direction explicit.

heddle

    • needsRedraw

      public void needsRedraw(boolean rescale)
      Signals that this canvas needs a repaint, optionally requesting a world rescale. Safe to call from any thread; the actual work happens on the next timer tick.
      Parameters:
      rescale - if true, the world system is recomputed before repainting

    • setWorldSystem

      public void setWorldSystem()
      Recomputes the world system from the current data and plot parameters.

      Handles manual limits, algorithmic (NiceScale) limits, and log-axis bounds. Activates log scaling only when the final data range is strictly positive.

    • screenToRawWorld

      public void screenToRawWorld(Point screenPoint, Point2D.Double rawPoint)
      Converts a screen (pixel) point to raw-world coordinates.

      Raw world is the coordinate system of _worldSystem. When log axes are active, raw world is in log₁₀(data) space. Use this for rubber-band zoom operations.

      Parameters:
      screenPoint - screen point in component coordinates (non-null)
      rawPoint - output point filled with raw-world coordinates (non-null)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if either argument is null

    • screenToRawWorld

      public void screenToRawWorld(Rectangle screenRect, Rectangle2D.Double rawRect)
      Converts a screen (pixel) rectangle to a raw-world rectangle.

      Use this for rubber-band zoom: the result can be assigned directly into _worldSystem.

      Parameters:
      screenRect - screen rectangle in component coordinates
      rawRect - output rectangle in raw-world coordinates (non-null)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if rawRect is null

    • screenToData

      public void screenToData(Point screenPoint, Point2D.Double dataPoint)
      Converts a screen (pixel) point to data coordinates (always linear units).

      Use this for mouse readouts and hit-tests in data space.

      dataPoint - output point in data coordinates (non-null)
      Throws:

    • screenToData

      public void screenToData(Rectangle screenRect, Rectangle2D.Double dataRect)
      Converts a screen rectangle to data-space bounds (always linear units).

      Do not use this to update _worldSystem; for zoom you want raw-world coordinates.

      Parameters:

      dataRect - output rectangle in data coordinates (non-null)
      Throws:

    • dataToScreen

      public boolean dataToScreen(Point screenPt, Point2D.Double dataPoint)
      Converts a data point (linear units) to screen (pixel) coordinates.

      Handles log-axis conversion internally (data → log₁₀ → raw-world → screen).

      Parameters:
      screenPt - output screen point (non-null)
      dataPoint - input data point in linear units (non-null)
      Returns:
      true on success; false if the point is invalid for the current axes (e.g. non-positive on a log axis) or transforms are unavailable

    • dataToScreen

      Parameters:

      dataRect - input data rectangle in linear units (non-null)
      Returns:
      true on success; false if any corner is invalid for the current axes or transforms are unavailable
